note: Elytra flight cannot be driven headlessly: gliding is player bound, there is no command that makes an entity fall-fly on demand with a controlled pitch, and the elytra branch of LivingEntity#travel only runs on the instance that controls the entity. So these vectors are hand derived from the decompiled and unobfuscated trees under mc-pipeline/work/<id>/src/ rather than measured on a live server. Every constant below names the class and method it was read from and the versions it holds for. Cases of type steady-glide and steady-cruise additionally carry an independent closed form solved by hand from the same equations, so the simulator is checked against algebra rather than against itself; those carry a relative tolerance of 1e-5 because the closed forms use exact 0.99 and 0.98 while the game (and the reimplementation) widen float literals to 0.9900000095367432 and 0.9800000190734863. Cases of type flight, dive-then-level, and travel are per tick runs of the same cited physics, pinned as regressions. Cross check against the projectile physics the pipeline did measure on a live server (mc-pipeline/vectors/projectile, method rcon-e2e, exact per tick Motion read back over RCON): an arrow launched at 3.0 blocks per tick comes back from the real server at 2.9700000286102295, which is 3 * fround(0.99) and not 3 * 0.99. The elytra multiplies by the same float literals in the same place, so the arithmetic layer these vectors rest on is confirmed against a real server even though the elytra branch itself cannot be. vectors.test.ts asserts that cross check directly.

model.tickOrder: Per simulated tick the firework rocket boost is applied first (FireworkRocketEntity#tick, attached branch) and then the glide step (LivingEntity#travel elytra branch, LivingEntity#updateFallFlyingMovement from 1.21.11). The game ticks the player entity and the rocket entity separately, so real order differs by a one tick phase shift; the displacement per tick at steady state is identical either way because move() consumes the post-drag delta in both orderings.
assumptions: Yaw is constant, so the flight is a vertical plane and distance means horizontal distance along the heading.
Pitch is the player xRot in degrees: positive looks down.
No blocks, no water, no wind, no collisions; horizontalCollision never fires so the fly-into-wall damage path is never taken.
Flights start from rest unless a case says otherwise.
Rocket lifetime is evaluated at the mean of its 0 to 11 tick jitter; min and max are reported as a spread, never sampled randomly.

constants.name: gravity
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel local (1.16.5, 1.18.2), Entity#getGravity backed by Attributes#GRAVITY with default 0.08 (1.20.6 onward), read through LivingEntity#getEffectiveGravity in 1.21.11 and 26.2

constants.name: slowFallingGravity
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel sets gravity to 0.01 under Slow Falling (1.16.5, 1.18.2); Math.min(gravity, 0.01) from 1.20.6 onward

constants.name: dragHorizontal
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel elytra branch, Vec3#multiply(0.99F, 0.98F, 0.99F)

constants.name: dragVertical
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel elytra branch, Vec3#multiply(0.99F, 0.98F, 0.99F)

constants.name: liftFactor
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel elytra branch: deltaY += gravity * (-1.0 + cos(pitch)^2 * 0.75). 1.16.5 evaluates the cosine through Mth#cos (float sine table); 1.18.2 onward use Math.cos. The 1.16.5 through 1.21.1 form also multiplies by Math.min(1.0, lookLength / 0.4), which is a no-op because the look vector is a unit vector; 1.21.11 dropped it and wrote Mth#square(Math.cos(pitch)).

constants.name: diveConversion
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel elytra branch: when deltaY < 0, convert = deltaY * -0.1 * lift, added to Y and spread along the horizontal look direction

constants.name: climbTrade
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel elytra branch: when pitch < 0, convert = horizontalSpeed * -Mth.sin(pitch) * 0.04, subtracted from the horizontal look direction

constants.name: climbVerticalGain
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel elytra branch: the same convert term is added to Y multiplied by 3.2

constants.name: steerRate
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#travel elytra branch: horizontal velocity is moved 10 percent toward (lookHorizontal / |lookHorizontal|) * preStepHorizontalSpeed

constants.name: boostAdd
constants.provenance: FireworkRocketEntity#tick attached branch: v += look * 0.1 + (look * 1.5 - v) * 0.5

constants.name: boostTarget
constants.provenance: FireworkRocketEntity#tick attached branch

constants.name: boostPull
constants.provenance: FireworkRocketEntity#tick attached branch

constants.name: boostFixedPoint
constants.provenance: Solving v = 0.5v + 0.85 from the boost recurrence: the rocket alone drives velocity toward look * 1.7 blocks per tick

constants.name: lifetimePerLevel
constants.provenance: FireworkRocketEntity constructor: lifetime = 10 * (1 + flightDuration) + nextInt(6) + nextInt(7)

constants.name: ticksPerDurability
constants.provenance: LivingEntity#updateFallFlying: (fallFlyTicks + 1) % 20 == 0 in 1.16.5; from 1.18.2 the same rate written as a 10 tick game event with damage on every second one

constants.name: elytraMaxDamage
constants.provenance: Items#ELYTRA Item.Properties.durability(432); confirmed from the extracted minecraft:max_damage component for 1.20.6 onward

constants.name: flightCutoffDamage
constants.provenance: ElytraItem#isFlyEnabled requires damage < maxDamage - 1 (1.16.5 through 1.21.1); LivingEntity#canGlideUsing requires !ItemStack#nextDamageWillBreak from 1.21.11, the same threshold. So an elytra refuses to glide once damage reaches 431 and 431 durability points are usable.

constants.name: unbreakingSkipChance
constants.provenance: DigDurabilityEnchantment#shouldIgnoreDurabilityDrop takes the 60 percent armor penalty only when the item is an ArmorItem, and ElytraItem extends Item through 1.21.1. From 1.21.1 on the data driven unbreaking.json applies its armor branch only to #minecraft:enchantable/armor, and the elytra sits in #minecraft:enchantable/durability but not in that armor tag. Either way the elytra gets the full non-armor skip rate.

constants.name: repairPerMembrane
constants.provenance: AnvilMenu#createResult restores min(damage, maxDamage / 4) per repair material; 432 / 4 = 108. ElytraItem#isValidRepairItem accepts the phantom membrane through 1.21.1, and the minecraft:repairable component names it from 1.21.11.

constants.name: mendingDurabilityPerXp
constants.provenance: ExperienceOrb repairs 2 durability per point of experience absorbed

constants.name: gliderComponentBoundary
constants.provenance: 1.21.1 and earlier gate gliding on Items.ELYTRA plus ElytraItem#isFlyEnabled inside LivingEntity#updateFallFlying. 1.21.11 and 26.2 gate it on LivingEntity#canGlideUsing, which requires the data driven DataComponents.GLIDER plus a matching EQUIPPABLE slot. The extracted item component dumps agree: minecraft:glider is absent for 1.20.6 and 1.21.1 and present for 1.21.11 and 26.2. The exact release inside the 1.21.2 to 1.21.10 gap is not on disk, so the boundary is stated as a bracket.

cases.provenance: FireworkRocketEntity#tick recurrence v' = 0.5v + 0.85 solved for its fixed point

Closed form of the pitch 0 fixed point with lift = 1: vy = -0.02 * 0.882 / (1 - 0.882) and vh = 0.99 * 0.9 * (-0.1 * (vy - 0.02)) / 0.01, both solved by hand from LivingEntity#travel. This is the terminal glide speed with no rockets.
Per tick run of the cited glide physics, pinned as a regression

Closed form of the pitch 0 fixed point with the rocket boost applied every tick: vy = -0.02 * 0.882 / (1 - 0.441) and vh = 0.99 * (0.85 + 0.9 * -0.1 * (0.5 vy - 0.02)) / 0.505. This is the chained rocket cruise speed, 33.45 blocks per second, and it is the number the community quotes as roughly 33.5 metres per second.
